products.name: Physical Intelligence (pi0)
products.note: General-purpose robot AI; physical task learning; safety-critical; emerging governance standards

reading.body:
Physical Intelligence builds general-purpose robot models trained on multi-robot, multi-task data to control any robot on any physical task, placing compute demands directly into the physical world where energy and cooling infrastructure will become critical constraints.

The company's progression from π0 to π0.5 reflects a pattern common to frontier AI: scaling data collection and model capacity to achieve generalization across new environments without retraining. This approach mirrors large language model scaling but with a harder constraint: every training step requires physical robots operating in real space, consuming electricity and generating heat. As these models grow more capable, the buildings housing training fleets and the power supplying them become direct inputs to capability gains, not downstream consequences.

Physical task learning differs from digital AI in one crucial way for infrastructure. A language model runs on a server farm. A robot policy runs on servers and on robots distributed across warehouses, factories, and homes. The compute footprint is thus split between centralized training infrastructure and decentralized deployment hardware, both consuming power. This distributed physical presence means that scaling robot AI may encounter power bottlenecks sooner than scaling digital AI, since deployment sites often lack the dedicated infrastructure of data centers.

The data provided covers the company's product focus and technical approach but does not address its training infrastructure, power consumption, facility locations, or deployment scale. Without those details, the extent to which Physical Intelligence will face grid constraints remains unclear.

profile_text.body:
Physical Intelligence is a company focused on bringing general-purpose AI into the physical world. Its team includes engineers, scientists, roboticists, and company builders who develop learning algorithms intended to produce a model capable of controlling any robot to perform any task.

The company's primary AI work centers on generalist robot policies. Its first such model, π0, combined large-scale multi-task and multi-robot data collection with a new network architecture, which the company describes as enabling the most capable and dexterous generalist robot policy to date. A subsequent model, π0.5, extends π0 with what the company calls open-world generalization, demonstrated through a mobile manipulator that can clean up an entirely new kitchen or bedroom without prior exposure to that environment. The site tracks π0 under the emerging and frontier AI category, noting its relevance to physical task learning, safety-critical applications, and emerging governance standards.

No litigation, SEC filings, patent records, or MCP server registrations are present in the available data for Physical Intelligence.
